m:mercado: Open Monday–Saturday from 7:30am to 3pm; closed on Sundays and public holidays (visitvalencia.com). Entry is free. The best time is the morning, before 1pm: after 2pm many stalls start to close.
m:lonja: Open Monday–Saturday 10am–7pm, Sunday and holidays 10am–2pm. Entry €2 (€1 reduced), free on Sundays and holidays (visitvalencia.com and guides). Closed on 1 and 6 January, 1 May and 25 December. If the tower climb is open, it's the same ticket: ask at the desk.
m:seu: Cathedral visit: Monday–Friday 10:30am–6:30pm (last entry 5:30pm), Saturday 10:30am–5:30pm (last entry 4:30pm), Sunday and holidays 2–5:30pm (last entry 4:30pm). Ticket €12, €6 reduced, with audio guide (visitvalencia.com). Closed to visits on 1 and 6 January, 19 March, Palm Sunday, Good Friday, 9 October, and 8 and 25 December. The Miguelete has a separate ticket, about €2 according to guides (to be confirmed), and is open every day 10am–6:45pm; there are about 200 narrow steps and no lift.
m:carmen: The streets are free to wander. Torres de Serranos and Torres de Quart: Monday–Saturday 10am–7pm, Sunday and holidays 10am–2pm, last entry 30 minutes before closing (valencia.es). Entry about €2 per tower, free on Sundays (price from a guide, to be confirmed). Closed on 1 and 6 January, 1 May and 25 December. Climbing Serranos means narrow, steep stairs.
m:cac: Walking around the area and seeing the buildings from outside is free. The interiors are paid separately: the combined Oceanogràfic + Science Museum + Hemisfèric ticket costs €47.75 (€14 less for children and over-65s; Visit València website). For the Hemisfèric you must arrive on time: once the screening has started you can't go in. From Alameda it's about 20 minutes on foot.
m:turia: Always free. After heavy rain the park may be closed or flooded: if there's a weather alert, go up to street level. In summer look for shade: the central stretches have little.
m:bellas: Open Tuesday–Sunday 10am–8pm, closed on Mondays; on 24 and 31 December 10am–2pm; closed on 1 January and 25 December. Free entry (valencia.es).
m:colon: Stalls and shops 7:30am–3pm; cafés and restaurants stay open longer (guides). The station and the square are free to see.
m:ruzafa: The market is open Monday–Saturday 7:30am–2:30pm. Many venues open later and close in the afternoon: the evening is the liveliest time.
m:ocean: Adult ticket (ages 13–64) from €39.45 according to the ticketing website (price varies with the season, to be confirmed); the combined ticket with the Science Museum and Hemisfèric costs €47.75. Open every day: normally 10am–6pm (Monday–Friday and Sunday) and 10am–8pm on Saturdays and in high season; on 24 and 31 December 10am–4pm (approximate hours, to be confirmed). Last entry an hour before closing.
m:malvarrosa: The beach is open and free. The lifeguard service normally runs from 7 June to 7 September: out of season swimming is unsupervised. Many places on the seafront are aimed at tourists; to eat for less, head towards the Cabanyal. From the centre you can get there by tram (lines 4 and 6, about 15–20 minutes).
vd:santacat: A historic horchatería on the little Santa Catalina square, near the Lonja: have horchata, a cold drink made from tiger nuts (chufa), with fartons, sweet sticks for dipping. In winter there's also hot chocolate with churros.
vp:santacat: Budget range, about €7 per person for horchata and fartons (menu not seen). Hours from a Time Out listing, to be confirmed.
vd:centralbar: Chef Ricard Camarena's tapas counter inside the Central Market: hot sandwiches (bocadillos) and simple dishes made with produce from the stalls. The squid bocadillo is the best known; eat standing at the counter, with a caña or a vermouth.
vp:centralbar: Budget range (menu not seen). Closed on Sundays. Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
vd:rincon: A Mediterranean restaurant right opposite the market, using fish and vegetables from the nearby stalls. Open from breakfast to evening: good for a rice lunch or a break between stops.
vp:rincon: Mid-range (menu not seen). Hours from Visit València, to be confirmed.
vd:pilareta: A Valencian tapas bar in El Carmen, known for clóchinas, Valencia's small mussels (in season, mainly May to August), to eat with a caña at the little tables.
vp:pilareta: Budget range (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays. Hours from an online listing; I couldn't find the afternoon break: check the day before.
vd:casamontana: A Cabanyal bodega open for generations: tinned fish, garlic prawns, grilled sardines and Valencian tapas with a long wine list. It's the place for a proper dinner in the fishermen's quarter.
vp:casamontana: Upper-mid range: about €20–35 per person according to one guide, up to €40 according to Visit València (menu not seen). Closed on Sunday evenings. Bookings by phone only.
vd:carmela: Wood-fired paella made to order, in the Valencian tradition: with chicken, rabbit and vegetables, or with seafood. It's a long lunch, near the beach: book ahead, even a week in advance at weekends.
vp:carmela: Higher range than the other places: about €25–50 per person for paella (different guides give different prices; menu not seen). Closed on Mondays, lunch only. Phone to book: 96 371 00 73.
vd:bunyols: A small fritter shop in Ruzafa where you can try bunyols de carabassa, pumpkin fritters typical of autumn and winter, with a cup of hot chocolate. Cash only.
vp:bunyols: Budget range (menu not seen). Cash only. Hours from an online listing: Saturday and Sunday afternoons only.
vd:cafemadrid: The bar where agua de Valencia was invented in 1959, a cocktail of cava, orange juice, gin and vodka. Order a jug to share between two, with something to nibble: it's the most Valencian aperitif there is.
vp:cafemadrid: Budget range (menu not seen). Closed on Mondays, open only from 5pm. Hours from an online listing, to be confirmed.
cd:ciencias: An interactive museum in the City of Arts and Sciences.
cd:hemisferic: An eye-shaped dome cinema, in the City of Arts and Sciences.
cd:bioparc: A zoo without bars, where animals live in African landscapes.
cd:quart: The city's medieval gate, with walls you can climb.
cd:ceramica: Ceramics in a Baroque palace with an alabaster portal.
cd:fallero: The figures saved from the Fallas bonfires, from 1934 to today.
cd:albufera: Half an hour on the lake, among the rice fields, at sunset.
cx:albufera: It's in El Palmar, about 12 km from the centre.
